Easter Celebrations – *Óbidos Holy Week celebrations in Óbidos date back to the 17th century. Held from Good Friday to Easter Sunday, the solemn religious ceremonies include traditional re-enactments, Masses and torchlight processions. Attracting thousands of visitors and devotees every year, the cultural program also includes art and sculpture exhibitions, musical performances and guided tours of the historical town. Peixe em Lisboa (Lisbon Fish & Flavours) – Pátio da Galé – Terreiro do Paço Lisbon Fish and Flavours is a popular food festival celebrating one of the main culinary specialities of the city – fish – which is skilfully prepared in a mouth-watering number of combinations and flavours. Wander around the exhibition stands to buy gourmet products, enjoy talks and tastings, watch cooking demonstrations and savour gastronomic delights created by Portugal’s most celebrated chefs.

Jazz in Lisbon – Lisbon/Estoril – May to September The arrival of summer is Lisbon is marked by a number of regular jazz concerts. Out Jazz is a series of free open-air concerts in the city’s beautiful parks and gardens every Sunday evening while Jazz às 5ªs is held every Thursday at the Centro Cultural de Belém. Estoril Jazz is a major week-long event for jazz aficionados, attracting a host of acclaimed musicians and groups to the cosmopolitan coastal resort of Estoril. Lisbon International Triathlon – Parque das Nações Held at the futuristic Parque das Nações along the riverfront, the Lisbon International Triathlon attracts over 800 participants from 30 countries. The spectator-friendly swim course is held in a unique artificial lake, the bicycle course offers inspiring views of the Tagus river and the running course is held in the heart of the venue.

Alkantara Festival – May/June The Alkantara Festival is an international biennial dedicated to the performing arts. During the course of this festival, many of Lisbon’s concert halls, theatres, squares and parks are filled with music, theatre and dance performances. The diverse programme of cultural events attracts performers from Portugal, all over Europe and many other parts of the world. Don’t miss out on the passion and drama of Alkantara Festival! Sintra Festival – Sintra – May/June For two weeks the summer, classical music fills the concert halls, manor houses and historical palaces of enchanting Sintra. The Sintra Festival is a celebration of music, dance, theatre and cultural events featuring international pianists, conductors and musicians as well as local ensembles. Events are held in some of the most beautiful venues in Lisbon, including the National Palace of Queluz, the National Palace of Sintra and the Centro Cultural Olga Cadaval.

O modelo funciona há 45 anos no país de origem e procura, sobretudo, privilegiar a grande proximidade entre a gastronomia e os consumidores locais. O regresso do Guia Repsol tem o objetivo de enaltecer a gastronomia portuguesa, que a diretora da marca acredita estar a viver um “momento excecional”. Ainda no primeiro semestre de 2025 vão abrir-se as hostilidades dos festivais dedicados aos caracóis, com o maior certamente a acontecer em Loures, entre 1 de maio e 27 de junho. Durante o mesmo mês, Lisboa irá acolher o Heróis do Mar, um recente festival que, durante quatro dias, celebra o peixe e o marisco, o “melhor que o oceano oferece a Portugal”. Junho é o mês da sardinha, da bifana no pão e dos santos populares. Não faltarão festas na rua um pouco por todo o País. No mês seguinte é altura de rumar a Idanha-a-Nova para mais uma edição do Arrebita, o festival que junta diversos chefs de renome.

Logo a seguir, entre 28 e 30 de março, celebra-se a Feira da Foda. O evento é, claro, dedicado ao Cordeiro à Moda de Monção — uma das 7 Maravilhas Gastronómicas de Portugal. A especialidade da iniciativa, também conhecida como “Foda à Monção”, vai ser a protagonista, mas há muito mais para conhecer além do cordeiro. Por lá irá encontrar expositores com vinhos da região e artesanato regional, espaços exclusivos para os produtores de gado e máquinas agrícolas, sem esquecer as “demonstrações de tosquias e muita animação popular com ranchos folclóricos, grupos de bombos, tocadores de concertina, charangas e DJ. O cordeiro que serve na freguesia de Pias, em Monção. Abril será marcado pelo regresso do festival Sangue na Guelra, que se divide entre tertúlias, festival de comida de rua e jantares feitos pelos sous chefs e/ou os números dois dos restaurantes.
Para fechar as hostilidades, o evento gastronómico do País regressa Santarém regressa para a sua 44.ª edição entre 27 de outubro e 5 de novembro.

2025 ainda agora começou e já se adivinham vários momentos impactantes para o cenário da gastronomia portuguesa. Desde a segunda Gala Michelin aos festivais regionais com pratos típicos, há muito para explorar e provar ao longo dos próximos 12 meses. Para que ninguém fique perdido e possa planear as férias de acordo com o apetite, a NiT criou um guia para ser mais fácil apontar tudo na agenda. E o ano arranca desde logo com várias festas do fumeiro no norte do País. Os fãs de enchidos poderão provar as especialidades em Boticas (9 de janeiro), Montalegre (23 de janeiro) e Macedo de Cavaleiros (30 de janeiro). Cada região irá apresentar diferentes propostas feitas pelos cozinheiros da zona. Com um total de 17 salas e 2 auditórios disponíveis para aluguer, proporciona uma variedade significativa de espaços para eventos, que podem acomodar desde congressos até festas empresariais e reuniões. A música de concerto, também conhecida como música clássica ou música erudita, é uma forma predominante de música enraizada nas tradições ocidentais seculares e litúrgicas. A cidade tem uma cena musical vibrante e animada, com muitos espaços para ouvir música ao vivo em diversos géneros, desde o fado português até ao jazz e rock internacional. Fado em Alfama Um dos géneros musicais mais emblemáticos de Portugal é o fado, e não há melhor lugar para o ouvir do que em Alfama, um dos bairros mais antigos e pitorescos de Lisboa. Vários restaurantes e casas de fado oferecem espetáculos ao vivo todas as noites, acompanhados de comida deliciosa e vinho português. O Coala Festival regressa a Cascais para a sua terceira edição portuguesa, nos dias 30 e 31 de Maio, afirmando-se como o arranque oficioso da temporada de festivais. # What’s on: A Review of MAAT’s Summer 2019 Collections

#### [Eden Flaherty](https://www.atlaslisboa.com/author/eden-flaherty/)

A review of the summer exhibitions at MAAT and Edp Central. What's on display, and are they worth visiting?

This week saw another slightly awkward but generally enjoyable opening at [MAAT](https://www.atlaslisboa.com/maat-museum/), this time marking not one but five new exhibitions — three in MAAT and two in the old EDP factory. What should you expect from the new season? Are there any must-sees or has MAAT fallen short?

### Jesper Just. Servitudes – Circuits (Interpassivities)   16 May 2019 – 02 September 2019

The main MAAT exhibition space — the Oval Gallery — has been given over to a large-scale video installation by Jesper Just. By far the most structurally impressive exhibit that MAAT has hosted so far, it features walkways of scaffolding bypassing the main stairs, shooting you into the center of the large, open space. The looping videos that make up the installation are projected on the walls and sail-like sheets that hang throughout the space. On the opening night, the echoing of shoes on metal from the few people who walked the runways and the sparseness of the gallery itself mirrored the rather haunting nature of the videos, tying the piece together nicely. However, it is easy to see how this could quickly be turned on its head when the crowds roll in and the industrial walkways get congested with tour groups.

![MAAT Summer 2019 review](https://www.atlaslisboa.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/IMG_3097-e1558367354320-730x523.jpg)

### Carla Filipe. Amanhã Não Há Arte   16 May 2019 – 09 September 2019

I imagine this is what it would have looked like if Lenin had invented pop art — and I say that as a compliment. This interactive exhibit includes large painted drapes, copyrighted cushions, and a printed newspaper that compliments the pieces. Based on the artist’s long study of protest banners, the exhibition is made up of symbols and graphics taken from the “political post-25 April 1974 narrative,” and the name of the installation, “Tomorrow there will be no Art,” is a cry for help against the challenges faced by the artistiwc community.

I call it “interactive” because people were lounging on the cushions while admiring the banners, which are composites of many images and hang like giant LSD blotters in the smaller MAAT side room. And you are able to take the paper with you as a sort of souvenir. The massive sails of color stand in stark relief to the transparent sheets of the Oval Gallery, and walking from the rather grey main exhibit into this one is like a slap to the face.

![MAAT Summer 2019 review Carla Filipe. Amanhã Não Há Arte](https://www.atlaslisboa.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/IMG_3106-e1558367497300-350x467.jpg)

### Prémio Novos Artistas Fundação EDP   16 May 2019 – 09 September 2019

If you head over to EDP Central, the new main exhibit is a compilation of the winners of the EDP new artists competition. The variety of pieces are slightly disjointed, sometimes don’t work, but certainly show how the gallery is supporting artists in their upward struggle to a career in the arts (see Amanhã Não Há Arte). However, it is clear that they are “emerging” artists, with the difference in quality clear when comparing the triptych photos in the Prémio Novos Artistas Fundação EDP to those in the “Fiction And Fabrication. Photography Of Architecture After The Digital Turn” exhibition in MAAT, which began in March, but is very much worth checking out.

This seems like the kind of exhibit that should be supported for what it represents, rather than what it is displaying.

### Pedro Tudela. Awdiˈtɔrju   16 May 2019 – 13 October 2019

This installation is in the Boiler Hall, which in and of itself is a spectacle. The piece’s most striking element is a row of modernized bells hanging from the ceiling, and the choice to place an auditory piece in this gallery is a fantastic one. By far the most abstract of the new exhibits, this would be a far less impressive display if not for its surroundings. That said, it makes the stroll through the dimly-lit hall very enjoyable and adds another dimension to the museum.

So, should you go to MAAT? Yes, absolutely. This is one of the rare times when all the galleries are open, and they pretty much all have something interesting to see. You can get combined tickets for EDP Central and MAAT, but if you only want to go to one, choose the latter.

Foodies, gastrónomos, chefs, restaurateurs e todos aqueles a quem a gastronomia interessa: eis os eventos a não perder. Festivais de talento, mercados de vinhos, debates de ideias, jantares a várias mãos, festas que celebram a diversidade de sabores e prémios para o que de melhor se faz por cá. **É o maravilhoso mundo da gastronomia portuguesa em eventos a acontecer nas próximas semanas.**

## O melhor da agenda na gastronomia

### Jantares especiais a sul

![Jantares especiais a sul](https://media.timeout.com/images/106250204/750/422/image.jpg "Jantares especiais a sul")

![Jantares especiais a sul](https://media.timeout.com/images/106250204/750/562/image.jpg "Jantares especiais a sul")

*DR*

Já não faltavam boas razões para rumar a sul para conhecer o novo Viceroy at Ombria Algarve, em Loulé, mas até Novembro há ainda quatro jantares únicos com chefs convidados que prometem deixar-nos de água na boca. O tiro de partida foi dado com Vasco Coelho Santos, chef do Euskalduna, uma estrela Michelin no Porto. Seguem-se Henrique Sá Pessoa, do Alma (duas estrelas Michelin), nos dias 11 e 12 de Julho, Alexandre Silva, do Loco (uma estrela Michelin), a 12 e 13 de Setembro, e Louise Bourrat, luso-francesa Boubou’s a 7 e 8 de Novembro. A curadoria é de Nelson Marques e o desafio é que o chef da casa, Pedro Pinto, apresente cinco pratos que celebrem a gastronomia algarvia e os convidados assinam outras cinco criações. Os jantares são limitados a 25 pessoas por noite e têm o preço de 225€ (com harmonização vínica).

# What’s on in June in Lisbon

#### [Ellis Dixon](https://www.atlaslisboa.com/author/ellisdixon/)

Sardines on the grill, pimba in the streets, and surprise parties around every corner.

June in Lisbon arrives with the smell of grilled sardines, the sound of double-entendre pimba music drifting through the streets, and the collective understanding that sleep is now very much optional. [Santo António season](https://www.atlaslisboa.com/st-anthony-marchas-populares/) officially peaks on the night of 12 June, but in reality, the city spends the entire month in celebration mode, with neighborhood *arraiais* spilling across squares, staircases, *miradouros*, and improbably steep streets from Alfama to Campolide. [Here’s a decent list of Santo António events to get you started](https://www.timeout.pt/lisboa/pt/coisas-para-fazer/arraiais-em-lisboa), but we just look for colorful streamers and follow wafting scents of freshly poured beer and grilled goodies. Arraiaias tend to find *you.*

Need some tips on [how to survive the festas](https://www.atlaslisboa.com/santos-populares/)? We got you.

Alongside the beer-fueled dancing and plastic basil pots, Lisbon’s cultural calendar is equally packed this year: archaeological film festivals, women-led clown cabarets, open-air cinema nights, experimental art exhibitions, literary gatherings, castle workshops, vintage markets, and enough live music to accidentally soundtrack your entire summer with unexpected accordions. In other words, if you were hoping for a quiet June in Lisbon, you’ve come to the wrong city.[](<>)

**June 5 and 6 | INTERNATIONAL FEMALE CLOWN FESTIVAL |** **Tem Graça |** **Orlando Ribeiro Library Auditorium | FREE**

Lisbon is about to get a little sillier — in the best possible way. The sixth edition of TEM GRAÇA, Portugal’s only international festival dedicated to women clowns and comedians, celebrates female-led humor from around the world. This year’s highlight is *The Red Cabaret*, a delightfully unpredictable variety show featuring performers from Portugal, Brazil, England, and France, blending clowning, magic, juggling, puppetry, and a healthy dose of mischief. Before the main event, audiences can experience an intimate five-minute peek-show performance by Brazilian artist Kelly Lima, promising secrets, laughter, and a few revelations through a very small window. Entry is free (subject to capacity), making this one of June’s most wonderfully eccentric outings. [Find out more here.](https://www.agendalx.pt/events/event/tem-graca-festival-internacional-de-mulheres-palhacas/)

**June 6 | FLEA MARKET | Feira das Almas – Anjos70 | Largo do Intendente | 11h – 19h | FREE**

Lisbon’s beloved Feira das Almas is turning 14, and naturally, it’s celebrating the only way it knows how: with vintage treasures, handmade oddities, good music, and a healthy dose of neighbourhood charm. Organised by the ever-creative crew behind Anjos70, the alternative market returns to its roots in Intendente for a full day of independent makers, local crafts, second-hand gems, workshops, and live performances. Expect the sort of atmosphere where you arrive intending to “just have a quick look” and somehow leave three hours later clutching a retro jacket, handmade earrings, and a vague desire to start up a ceramics hobby. [Click here for more information.](https://ma.to/event/feira-das-almas-06-jun-2026)

**to June 14 | BOOK FAIR | Feira do Livro | Marques de Pombal | FREE**

The Lisbon Book Fair returns to Eduardo VII Park, transforming the city’s green heart into a paradise for bookworms. With more than 2,200 events spread across 350 pavilions, the program goes well beyond browsing the latest reads. Expect author signings, book launches, lively debates, live music on Friday evenings, and even dedicated silent reading sessions for those who prefer their literary adventures a little less social. If you’re looking for an excuse to spend an afternoon among books, this annual Lisbon institution is worth checking out. [Read more here.](https://feiradolivrodelisboa.pt/)

**June 18 – 21 | ARCHEOLOGICAL FILM FESTIVAL | MOCA – São Jorge Cinema | 3 – 30€**

History buffs, curious minds, and aspiring time travellers, take note: Lisbon’s first-ever MOCA Archaeological Film Festival is digging deep into the past with almost 30 films and documentaries exploring archaeology, heritage, and the stories buried beneath our feet. Expect everything from sweeping historical epics to thoughtful art-house gems, plus talks, workshops, family-friendly activities, and even a Roman-inspired dinner for those who like their history served with a side of food. Whether you’re an archaeology enthusiast or simply fancy a different kind of cinema experience, MOCA proves that the past is anything but static. [Get the full list of activities and buy tickets here](https://moca.bol.pt/).

**to June 30+ | OUTDOOR FILM SCREENING | Cine Society | Carmo Rooftop and Principe Real Garden + | 14,50€**

From timeless romances like *Casablanca*, *Roman Holiday*, and *It’s a Wonderful Life* to wonderfully offbeat adventures such as *Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas* and *Edward Scissorhands*, June’s open-air cinema lineup has something for almost every mood. There are slick modern crowd-pleasers too, including *Ocean’s 11*, *Live and Let Die*, and *The Hunger Games*, all screened under Lisbon’s summer sky. The ticket prices may make your wallet wince a little, but there’s no denying the appeal of watching a classic film with a warm evening breeze and a drink in hand. [Browse the program](https://shop.cinesociety.pt/?utm_source=societylisboa.beehiiv.com&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=society-lisboa), pick your favorites, and block out a few nights in your calendar before the seats disappear.

**to Aug 23 | ART EHXIBITION | Drifting Signals | Museum of Communication | FREE**

What exactly counts as communication in 2026? Drifting Signals, Lasting Traces, a new group exhibition at Lisbon’s Museum of Communications, takes that question and runs off-grid with it. Bringing together artists from Portugal and the U.K., the show explores the more niche systems of exchange that go beyond screens and pings — from underground plant networks and physical memory to invisible digital infrastructures and fleeting human connections. The show mixes installation, visual art, and more to investigate what lingers after messages are sent, missed, or transformed and invites you to slow down and pay attention to the signals you might normally overlook. [Read more here.](https://aeainitiative.com/drifting_signals_lasting_traces/)

**June 28 | CASTLE VISIT | Sundays at the Castle | Castelo São Jorge | 10h | FREE – 14€**

History lessons tend to be a lot more fun when they happen inside an actual medieval castle. From May through October, São Jorge Castle’s Sundays at the Castle series transforms the hilltop landmark into a playground for curious families, with interactive activities designed to bring Lisbon’s past vividly back to life. Expect storytelling, hands-on workshops, and guided experiences that make wandering ancient stone walls feel a little more magical than usual. The events take place on the last Sunday of each month, with activities included in the standard castle ticket — though some workshops and audio-described tours require advance booking before the tiny historians snap up all the spots. [Get more information here.](https://castelodesaojorge.pt/agenda/domingos-no-castelo-31-de-maio/)

Check out more Atlas picks for things to do around Lisbon year-round in our [events calendar](https://www.atlaslisboa.com/events-2/).
